questions.question: What is a business requirement?

choices.A: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product
choices.B: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.C: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.D: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.E: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.F: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems

questions.explanation: A business requirement states the objective the organization is trying to reach by having the product built.

questions.question: What is a business rule?

choices.A: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.B: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.C: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.D: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.E: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.F: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business

questions.explanation: A business rule comes from how the business operates. It often leads to software requirements but is not itself one.

questions.question: What is a constraint?

choices.A: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.B: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.C: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.D: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.E: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.F: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product

questions.explanation: A constraint narrows the set of design or implementation choices the developer is allowed to make.

questions.question: What is an external interface requirement?

choices.A: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.B: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.C: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems
choices.D: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.E: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.F: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system

questions.explanation: External interface requirements cover connections to users, other software systems, and hardware devices.

questions.question: What is a feature?

choices.A: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.B: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.C: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.D: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.E: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.F: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems

questions.explanation: A feature groups related capabilities and is normally described by several functional requirements.

questions.question: What is a functional requirement?

choices.A: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.B: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.C: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.D: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.E: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.F: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system

questions.explanation: A functional requirement states what the system does, under what condition, in terms a developer can build against.

questions.question: What is a nonfunctional requirement?

choices.A: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product
choices.B: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.C: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.D: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.E: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems
choices.F: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system

questions.explanation: Nonfunctional requirements describe properties and restrictions rather than behavior the system carries out.

questions.question: What is a quality attribute?

choices.A: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.B: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems
choices.C: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.D: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.E: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.F: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect

questions.explanation: A quality attribute is one kind of nonfunctional requirement, covering service characteristics like performance or security.

questions.question: What is a system requirement?

choices.A: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.B: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.C: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems
choices.D: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.E: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.F: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business

questions.explanation: System requirements apply to a whole product made of interacting parts, which may include hardware as well as software.

questions.question: What is a user requirement?

choices.A: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.B: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.C: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.D: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.E: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product
choices.F: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition

questions.explanation: User requirements describe what a user needs to accomplish, not the detailed software behavior that supports it.

questions.question: SCWW tells Liminal it wants to cut the time the office spends rebuilding job schedules by hand. What type of requirement is this?

choices.C: Business rule
choices.D: Constraint
choices.E: Business requirement
choices.F: Functional requirement

questions.explanation: This states why the organization wants Paarth and what value it expects, so it is a business requirement.

questions.question: Company policy says an employee who passes forty hours in a week earns overtime. What is the policy itself?

choices.C: Business rule
choices.D: Feature
choices.E: Functional requirement
choices.F: Quality attribute

questions.explanation: The overtime policy exists whether or not Paarth exists. Paarth may need functional requirements to enforce it.

questions.question: Paarth must run on the Raspberry Pi already installed in the shop office. What is the MOST specific classification?

choices.C: Constraint
choices.D: External interface requirement
choices.E: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.F: Business requirement

questions.explanation: Existing hardware removes implementation options from the developer, which is what a constraint does.

questions.question: Paarth must push each scheduled job into the shop's Google Calendar. What does the Google Calendar connection represent?

choices.C: Constraint
choices.D: Business rule
choices.E: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.F: External interface requirement

questions.explanation: Google Calendar is a separate software system Paarth has to communicate with.

questions.question: Payroll Management covers hour totals, overtime, mileage, and reimbursements. What is Payroll Management best classified as?

choices.C: Business rule
choices.D: System requirement
choices.E: Business requirement
choices.F: Quality attribute

questions.explanation: It names a group of related capabilities that deliver value together, which is a feature.

questions.question: When an employee scans an RFID card, Paarth shall record the clock-in time. What type of requirement is this?

choices.C: Feature
choices.D: Business rule
choices.E: Quality attribute
choices.F: User requirement

questions.explanation: It names a specific behavior triggered by a specific condition.

questions.question: Paarth should stay responsive with twenty employees using it at once. What is the MOST specific classification?

choices.C: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.D: Business rule
choices.E: Functional requirement
choices.F: External interface requirement

questions.explanation: Performance under load is a service characteristic, so quality attribute is more specific than nonfunctional requirement.

questions.question: A new office employee must be able to create a job correctly on their first attempt without being shown how. Which quality attribute is this?

choices.C: Integrity
choices.D: Reliability
choices.E: Maintainability
choices.F: Efficiency

questions.explanation: Usability covers how easily a user can learn the system and complete a task correctly.

questions.question: A shop manager needs to find out which production stage a given staircase is in. What type of requirement is this?

choices.C: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.D: User requirement
choices.E: Business requirement
choices.F: Constraint

questions.explanation: It describes a task a user class needs to accomplish, without saying how the software provides it.

questions.question: Paarth shall prevent any account without the manager role from opening the payroll editor. What is this statement?

choices.C: Quality attribute
choices.D: Feature
choices.E: System requirement
choices.F: Functional requirement

questions.explanation: The company policy is the business rule. This statement is the software behavior that enforces it.

questions.question: Paarth's timeclock is an RFID reader, a Raspberry Pi, kiosk software, a web API, and a database working together. A requirement covering that whole arrangement is called what?

choices.C: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.D: User requirement
choices.E: Constraint
choices.F: Functional requirement

questions.explanation: The requirement applies to a product assembled from several interacting subsystems.

questions.question: Company policy states that only managers may change an employee's payroll record. What is that policy?

choices.C: Functional requirement
choices.D: External interface requirement
choices.E: Business rule
choices.F: Quality attribute

questions.explanation: The policy belongs to the business. Paarth then needs functional and security requirements that enforce it.

questions.question: Which of these are functional requirements for Paarth? Select all that apply.

choices.A: Paarth shall calculate an employee's total hours for the current pay week
choices.B: Paarth shall run on the Raspberry Pi already installed in the shop office
choices.C: Paarth shall move a job into the archive when its status becomes completed
choices.D: Paarth shall record a clock-in time when an employee scans an RFID card
choices.E: SCWW wants to cut the hours spent on payroll paperwork by thirty percent
choices.F: Paarth shall answer a job status lookup within two seconds under normal load

questions.explanation: The first three name behavior the software performs. The others are a quality attribute, a business requirement, and a constraint.

questions.question: Which of these are nonfunctional requirements? Select all that apply.

choices.A: Paarth shall produce a mileage reimbursement total for each pay period
choices.B: Paarth must keep accepting clock-ins when the internet connection drops out
choices.C: Paarth shall let a manager change the production stage of an existing job
choices.D: Paarth must remain available throughout the shop's posted hours of operation
choices.E: Paarth must keep payroll records readable only to accounts with a manager role
choices.F: Paarth must return a job search result within two seconds under normal load

questions.explanation: Performance, security, availability, and robustness describe characteristics. The other two describe behavior.

questions.question: Which of these are stated at the level of a user requirement? Select all that apply.

choices.A: The client shall subscribe to a Socket.IO room named for the job identifier
choices.B: The API shall respond with HTTP 201 once a new job record has been created
choices.C: The server shall write a PunchRecord document after each accepted RFID scan
choices.D: Office staff need to review each employee's mileage before payroll closes
choices.E: A salesperson needs to check where a customer's staircase is in production
choices.F: An employee needs to clock in at the start of a shift without office help

questions.explanation: The first three name goals a user class has. The others are system behavior stated for a developer.

questions.question: Which of these would be external interfaces for Paarth? Select all that apply.

choices.A: The RFID reader that sends card scans to the timeclock kiosk
choices.B: The Google Calendar API that Paarth pushes scheduled jobs into
choices.C: The company policy that defines when overtime pay begins
choices.D: The shop's label printer that Paarth prints job travelers on
choices.E: The email service Paarth sends weekly payroll summaries through
choices.F: The job scheduling module inside the Paarth backend itself

questions.explanation: External interfaces are software systems, hardware devices, and users outside the system. A policy is a business rule, and an internal module is not external.

questions.question: A feature and a functional requirement mean the same thing.
questions.explanation: A feature bundles related capabilities and is usually described by several functional requirements.

questions.question: A business rule can exist even if Paarth is never built.
questions.explanation: Business rules belong to the business. Software requirements may be written to enforce them.

questions.question: Every quality attribute is a nonfunctional requirement.
questions.explanation: A quality attribute is defined as one type of nonfunctional requirement.

questions.question: Every nonfunctional requirement is a quality attribute.
questions.explanation: Constraints and external interface requirements are also nonfunctional but are not quality attributes.

questions.question: "A manager needs to approve payroll" and "Paarth shall show managers an Approve Payroll button" sit at the same level.
questions.explanation: The first is a user goal. The second is a specific product behavior proposed to support it.

questions.question: A constraint reduces the number of implementation choices open to the developer.
questions.explanation: That is the defining idea behind a constraint.

questions.question: SCWW says: "I don't care how you build it, the office just needs to know right away when the shop changes a job's stage." Which statement is the USER requirement?

choices.A: Broadcast a job:update event over Socket.IO to every connected office client
choices.B: Deploy the Paarth backend to Render so the office can reach it from anywhere
choices.C: Store each job's current production stage in a MongoDB collection named jobs
choices.D: Add a POST /api/jobs/:id/status endpoint that accepts the new stage value
choices.E: Paarth shall cut the shop's administrative workload by roughly thirty percent
choices.F: Office staff need to see production status changes without refreshing the page

questions.explanation: A user requirement names what the user needs to accomplish and leaves the implementation open.

questions.question: For that same request, which statement is the best FUNCTIONAL requirement?

choices.A: Production visibility has been the shop's most requested improvement this year
choices.B: Paarth shall notify every connected office client when a job's stage changes
choices.C: Socket.IO is a good fit here because it falls back to long polling cleanly
choices.D: Office staff need visibility into the production stage of every active job
choices.E: SCWW wants better communication between the shop floor and the front office
choices.F: Real-time updates matter more to this business than historical reporting does

questions.explanation: It states observable system behavior without naming a business goal, a user goal, or a specific technology.

questions.question: Which sequence runs from the highest-level reason for Paarth down to detailed software behavior?

choices.A: User requirement, then functional requirement, then business requirement
choices.B: User requirement, then business requirement, then functional requirement
choices.C: Functional requirement, then user requirement, then business requirement
choices.D: Business requirement, then functional requirement, then user requirement
choices.E: Business requirement, then user requirement, then functional requirement
choices.F: Business rule, then business requirement, then external interface requirement

questions.explanation: Why the business wants it, then what users must accomplish, then what the system does.

questions.question: A single business requirement can give rise to several user requirements.
questions.explanation: One business objective usually breaks down into multiple user goals and many functional requirements.

questions.question: Nonfunctional requirements are optional and can be dropped if the schedule slips.
questions.explanation: They are requirements. Dropping one changes what the delivered product is required to be.
